name: Hooke’s microscopic description of cork cells
description: Robert Hooke described the small compartments visible in cork and called them cells or pores in Micrographia.

date.basis: Date of the cited publication or documented episode; not a claim that the underlying work began that year.

events.statement: Micrographia appeared in London in 1665 with Hooke’s description of cork compartments.
events.scope: Robert Hooke described the small compartments visible in cork and called them cells or pores in Micrographia.
events.caveats: This account of cork compartments did not assert the full later cell theory; the exact date of the observation is not established. Hooke described the cork compartments as empty; this is not an account of living cell contents.

evidence.supports: Dates the publication and describes the compartments.
Identifies the cork illustration and its publication in 1665.
